summary: ACCEPT. D3 cross-venue slot scope. THE CHANGE IS ONE PREDICATE: TradeIntent.broker_account_id == broker.id added to the in-flight half of _fetch_position_maps, plus two docstring corrections. 10 source lines, no scope creep. WHY THIS IS NOT A STRATEGY CHANGE, which is how it was originally framed and which I reviewed and initially accepted: three independent written sources already required it. (1) Operator decision reading A in the s82 fan-out design. (2) My own fleet-board note of 2026-08-26: 'Build consequence: duplicate-exposure alarms must be scoped PER VENUE'. (3) MOST DAMNING, the source itself at :1254 warned that 'widening that one to a second broker account would make v2 believe it is in position on Schwab when only the Webull fan-out leg is open, silently changing ENTRY behaviour' -- a hazard the code ALREADY HAD via the unscoped intent half. The comment read as a guard while describing the live defect. THE OLD DOCSTRING WAS ACTIVELY FALSE: it claimed the union was 'for the v2 broker account', which was true of the virtual_positions half and false of the intent half. That false contract is the most likely reason this survived earlier review -- anyone reading the contract instead of the query saw a correctly scoped union. Both docstrings are now corrected and state that the halves are INDEPENDENTLY scoped. VERIFIED BY EXECUTED MUTATION, NOT INSPECTION. I ran it myself in an isolated worktree after first PROVING module provenance (project_mai_tai.__file__ resolved into the worktree, not the operator's real checkout -- the Git Bash path-mangling trap that has produced false results here before). Baseline: 9 passed. Mutant, the D3 predicate deleted to restore the pre-fix venue-blind union: 1 failed, 8 passed, failing exactly as 'assert {ORBONLY: 1} == {}'. Restore hash-verified byte-identical at 4ebdf933c2b9948d7bfce1f608830476ad1363a526939ed2419a197b709a6c87. THE TEST IS A TRUE ONE-VARIABLE CONTROLLED PAIR with both outcomes reachable: a fan-out-account intent on symbol ORBONLY must be ABSENT while a primary-account intent on SCHWABINTENT must be PRESENT at qty 3, asserted by exact dict equality. That shape catches over-inclusion AND over-exclusion, so a mutant that filtered everything would also die. PRESERVED AND CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: reading A, the exit-only unions at :269 and :1565 which must never reach an entry decision, and _fetch_reportable_state which is deliberately separate and spans both accounts. MAGNITUDE, and stated as reachability NOT harm: 1,583 fan-out intents over 60 symbol-days in the 14-day window polluted the entry union, more than the strategy's own 1,438. Non-terminal window median 0.105s, mean 59.1s, max 3,331.8s -- most were too short to block anything and the harm lives in the tail. ⛔ THE SUPPRESSED-ENTRY COUNT IS COULD_NOT_TELL AND MUST NOT BE QUOTED AS 1,583: a suppressed entry writes no trade_intent row, and the entry position gates are bare returns with no retained marker. I earlier ran an overlap query returning '1 pair in 14 days' and nearly reported it; it counts entries that GOT THROUGH, the inverse of the question. Recorded so nobody repeats it. ⛔ THE POPULATION IS BOOKED UNDER live:orb, NOT live:webull_30s -- a webull-keyed query returns 0 and reads as 'no problem'. NOT MEASURED: only the focused reportable-state file was mutated; no full-suite run was performed by me for this mutant, and codex's reported repository run of 2,924 passed with 12 Postgres-fixture setup errors from an absent local DSN is taken on report, not verified.
